answer: At each wharf of the PoA ledger, a new agent stakes a unique cryptographic relic tied to a hardware attestation, logged in a willow‑rooted Merkle tree. Rewards vest in tiny epochs, and a rate‑limit contract releases only a fraction per epoch, forcing a Sybil farm to front‑load the full stake for every fake node before any payout. Because the stake cannot be reused and each epoch costs time and capital, the attacker’s expense rises linearly with the number of identities, rendering large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
